methodology: Offline build-class signatures. At runtime the page requests only the operator-supplied GitLab and this bundled file. GitLab ships Webpack assets whose filenames embed a content hash, so a set of asset paths that all load identifies a specific frontend build. A frontend build can be shared by several patch releases when only backend code changed between them, so a match resolves to a VERSION RANGE, not necessarily a single patch. Only the authenticated /api/v4/version endpoint yields the exact patch.

crossOriginChannels.assetPresence: Content-hashed asset paths probed with and load/error. Needs no CORS: only presence is observed, never content. Primary signal.
crossOriginChannels.graphqlQuerySchema: SHA-256 of the sorted anonymous Query-type field names. Readable cross-origin because /api/graphql sets Access-Control-Allow-Origin: *. Corroborating signal where collected.
crossOriginChannels.unavailable: /assets/webpack/manifest.json returns 200 but carries no Access-Control-Allow-Origin header, so its contents are NOT readable cross-origin.

corpus.note: Per-patch corpus deduplicated into frontend build classes, per edition. CE and EE have distinct asset sets and never group together. Each build probe set is proven not to be a subset of any other collected build (0 collisions), so no two corpus builds can be confused. A build released after collection may match the newest collected build of its minor line.

notes: Each build probe set is verified not to be a subset of any other collected build, so corpus builds cannot be confused.

No two collected builds can be confused, but a patch released after collection can serve the same assets as the newest collected patch of its minor line; the page keeps that later patch as a candidate.
